rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1, 2.3, 3 - the study reports its own airborne hyperspectral and thermal campaigns (three dates, 2012) over 192 olive plots, its own albedometer field measurements, and its own METRIC model runs at eleven pixel sizes.
rows.notes: The study only estimates ETc / crop water requirements with METRIC at different spatial resolutions and compares results among pixel sizes (Tables 1-4); it never establishes or tests an irrigation management strategy, never measures water applied, water saved or water productivity, and does not validate ET against field flux measurements (only albedo is validated against albedometers). It thus supports at most the precondition (estimating water requirements) of the claimed effect (increased water productivity), not the effect itself.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1, 2.3, 3 - own airborne campaigns, field albedo measurements and METRIC runs over olive orchards in southern Spain.
rows.notes: No yield or fruit/oil quality data are reported anywhere in the study; it quantifies ETc, Kco and energy balance components as a function of pixel size and discusses implications for water requirement estimation (Section 4, Conclusions). The link from RS-based water requirement estimation to optimised yield and quality is not tested; the study is upstream of the claimed crop-production effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a methodological sensitivity analysis of METRIC spatial resolution (5 m to 1 km) using airborne imagery over olive orchards; ET estimates are compared among resolutions rather than validated against ground ET measurements. Neither claim row (water productivity/conservation or yield/quality) is addressed by the study's own results.
